(A) The excerpt claims that emancipation was carried out in a way that favored the landlords, because the local commissions that put it into effect "were dominated by landlords." As a result the serfs got land but only limited freedom: they usually stayed tied to the village commune (mir) and had to make redemption payments to the government for almost fifty years.

(B) Russia's defeat in the Crimean War (1853-1856) showed the government how far behind Britain and France it had fallen. The serf-based army and economy could not match industrialized enemies, and Russia lacked railroads to move troops and supplies to the front. Alexander II decided that freeing the serfs was necessary to modernize the economy and build a stronger army. He also feared peasant revolts, and in 1856 he told the nobles it was better to abolish serfdom from above than to wait for it to be abolished from below.

(C) After the Revolution of 1905, Prime Minister Pyotr Stolypin's agrarian reforms (starting in 1906) let peasants leave the mir and consolidate their strips into private farms. The government had already ended redemption payments after the revolution. Stolypin hoped to create a class of prosperous, independent peasants who would support the tsar instead of joining revolutionaries, so the reforms were meant to answer both peasant land hunger and opposition to the regime. At the same time he used harsh repression, including field courts-martial that executed many suspected rebels.

input.essay:
(A) The excerpt claims that the serfs did not get a clean break from their situation after 1861. Even though they received land and some freedom, they had to make redemption payments to the government, and these payments were stretched out over almost fifty years. So emancipation left the former serfs paying for their land for a very long time.

(B) One development that helps explain emancipation is Russia's defeat in the Crimean War, which lasted from 1853 to 1856. Russia lost to Britain and France, and the war showed that the Russian army was badly equipped and could not move troops and supplies well because Russia had almost no railroads. The army was made up of serf conscripts and the economy was based on serf labor, so Alexander II and his advisers concluded that serfdom was holding Russia back as a great power. This pushed the government to free the serfs so that Russia could modernize and catch up with the West.

(C) After 1861 the Russian state responded to problems in different ways. The government made some reforms and later there was a Duma. These changes were meant to deal with the unhappiness in Russia and with people who were against the tsar. Over time the tsars tried different things, some reforming and some harsher, but there was still a lot of opposition by 1914.
